OR-E2.Description:
Bring Oriflame Pakistan product data into the system from a permitted, reliable source (or clearly labelled development fixtures until one is confirmed), with a minimal schema, idempotent synchronisation, provenance, and failure recording.

SCOPE:
- Permitted-source investigation and ADR covering access terms and image/content rights
- Minimal catalogue schema and Alembic migrations (no tenant tables)
- Replaceable Oriflame source adapter isolated in backend/app/integrations/oriflame/
- Idempotent upsert repositories keyed on stable source identifiers
- Catalogue sync service recording every run in catalogue_sync_runs, with safe retries
- Explicitly named development fixtures, impossible to load in production
- Command-line sync entry point (admin trigger follows in OR-E6)

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Storefront pages and public catalogue APIs (OR-E3)
- Admin UI (OR-E6)
- Scraping that bypasses authentication, anti-bot systems, access restrictions, or rate limits — never in scope

REFERENCE DOCS:
- docs/CATALOGUE-DATA.md
- backend/AGENT.md (Catalogue Integration, Initial Database Model)
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- docs/adr/README.md

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
- ADR-001 records the chosen source, its terms, and image/content usage rights (or records that none is confirmed and fixtures are used)
- alembic upgrade head creates the catalogue schema; downgrade is documented
- Running sync twice against the same input yields identical row counts
- Every imported product stores source_url and last_synced_at
- Failed runs are recorded with error detail and can be retried safely
- No fabricated products, SKUs, prices, ratings, reviews, or stock anywhere
- Backend gate passes: uv run ruff check backend && uv run ruff format backend && uv run mypy backend && uv run pytest

OR-E2.Summary: Investigate permitted catalogue sources and record ADR-001
OR-E2.Description:
Determine a permitted, reliable source for Oriflame Pakistan product data and images before any ingestion code is written.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- Investigate official APIs, product feeds, and authorised exports available to the store owner (consultant tools, partner feeds)
- Confirm with the owner: access method, terms of use, rate limits, and whether product images/descriptions may be commercially republished
- Create docs/adr/ADR-001-catalogue-data-source.md (Status, Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives) and add it to the docs/adr/README.md index
- Record: source type, fields available (id, SKU, name, description, price PKR, images, categories, variants, availability), sync cadence, authorised image hosts
- If no permitted source is confirmed: ADR status Proposed; decision is to proceed with development fixtures only

EFFORT: M (4 hours, plus owner response time)
PROJECT AREA: Docs / Research
DEPENDENCIES: OR-E1

TESTING CRITERIA:
- ADR-001 exists, is indexed, and states image/content rights explicitly
- Owner confirmation (or its absence) is recorded, not assumed

EDGE CASES:
- Source requires login or is protected by anti-bot measures: do not bypass; record as rejected alternative
- Images not licensed for reuse: decide to link out or omit images; never copy them
- Source lacks live inventory: record that availability will be labelled 'Availability not confirmed'
- Ask before using any paid service or API plan

Create the minimal catalogue schema with SQLAlchemy models and an Alembic migration.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- backend/app/models/: Product (id, source_id unique, sku, slug unique, name, description, price_pkr Numeric nullable, currency default PKR, source_url, last_synced_at, is_visible default true, is_featured default false, created_at, updated_at)
- ProductImage (product_id FK cascade, url, alt_text, position, source_url)
- Category (id, source_id unique, slug unique, name, parent_id self-FK nullable)
- product_categories association table (composite PK)
- CatalogueSyncRun (id, source, started_at, finished_at, status enum running/success/failed/partial, created_count, updated_count, unchanged_count, error_count, error_detail text)
- ProductVariant and ProductAvailability ONLY if ADR-001 confirms the source provides them; otherwise omit and note in backend/AGENT.md
- Indexes: products.slug, products.sku, products.source_id, category membership, name search (functional lower(name) index; full-text added in OR-E3)
- Alembic migration 002_catalogue_schema with reversible downgrade; every table gets ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with no policies (Supabase Data API lockdown, docs/DATABASE.md)

EFFORT: M (5 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Backend / Database
DEPENDENCIES: OR-004, OR-010

TESTING CRITERIA:
- upgrade head then downgrade -1 then upgrade head succeeds
- Unique constraints reject duplicate slug and duplicate source_id
- alembic check shows no model/migration drift
- No tenant columns or tables exist
- Test asserts RLS is enabled on every application table in public

EDGE CASES:
- Price absent from source: price_pkr NULL, never 0 or a guessed value
- Deleting a product cascades its images but not shared categories
- Slug collisions between different source products: deterministic suffix strategy documented and tested

Implement repository functions that upsert catalogue records keyed on stable source identifiers.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- backend/app/repositories/products.py, categories.py, sync_runs.py
- upsert_product(record) using PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (source_id) DO UPDATE; returns created/updated/unchanged outcome
- Unchanged detection: compare relevant fields so last_synced_at updates but updated_at only changes on real change
- Images replaced per product in one transaction (delete-then-insert or diff) without duplicates
- Category upsert by source_id; product-category links reconciled
- Repositories contain no HTTP or business logic

EFFORT: M (6 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Backend
DEPENDENCIES: OR-011

TESTING CRITERIA:
- Same record upserted twice: one row, second outcome 'unchanged'
- Changed price: outcome 'updated', price persisted
- Image list changes reflected exactly; no duplicate images after repeated upserts
- All queries parameterised (no string-built SQL)

EDGE CASES:
- Record missing source_id: rejected with validation error, counted as error, not inserted
- Category referenced before it exists: created or deferred deterministically, no FK violation
- Concurrent sync runs: second run refused (advisory lock) rather than racing

Define a source adapter interface and implement the adapter chosen in ADR-001 (or the fixture adapter only), isolated so the source can be replaced later.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- backend/app/integrations/oriflame/client.py: CatalogueSource Protocol with iter_products() and iter_categories() yielding validated Pydantic SourceProduct / SourceCategory models
- Permitted-source adapter (per ADR-001) using httpx with explicit timeouts, bounded retries with backoff for idempotent reads, and respect for documented rate limits
- FixtureCatalogueSource reading explicitly named development fixture files (OR-015)
- Source selection via settings (CATALOGUE_SOURCE=fixture|<permitted adapter name>); add to .env.example and docs
- Map source fields to SourceProduct including source_url; never fill missing fields with invented values

EFFORT: M (6 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Backend / Integration
DEPENDENCIES: OR-010, OR-002

TESTING CRITERIA:
- Adapter tests with mocked HTTP (respx or equivalent): parse success, timeout, 429, 5xx, malformed payload
- Pydantic validation rejects records missing required fields
- No test makes a real network call

EDGE CASES:
- 401/403 from source: stop the run and record failure; never attempt to bypass
- 429: honour Retry-After within a bounded budget, then fail the run
- Partial page failure: run marked partial with error detail
- Unknown CATALOGUE_SOURCE value: startup validation error

OR-E2.Summary: Catalogue sync service with run recording and safe retries
OR-E2.Description:
Orchestrate a full sync: read from the configured source, upsert via repositories, and record the run outcome.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- backend/app/integrations/oriflame/catalogue.py: CatalogueSyncService.run(source) creating a catalogue_sync_runs row (status running), processing categories then products, updating counts, finishing with success / partial / failed
- Per-record errors counted and summarised in error_detail (truncated, no secrets); run continues where safe
- Fatal errors (auth, source unreachable) end the run as failed
- Advisory lock prevents concurrent runs
- Stale-run recovery: runs stuck in running beyond a timeout are marked failed at next start
- structlog events catalogue_sync_started / finished / failed

EFFORT: M (6 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Backend
DEPENDENCIES: OR-012, OR-013

TESTING CRITERIA:
- Running the sync twice with the same fixture: identical product/category/image counts; second run all 'unchanged'
- Simulated mid-run failure: run recorded failed/partial; rerun completes without duplicates
- Concurrent run attempt rejected with clear message

EDGE CASES:
- Product removed from source: not hard-deleted; marked is_visible=false (or handled per ADR-001) and logged
- Source returns zero products unexpectedly: treat as suspicious, fail the run rather than hiding the whole catalogue
- Very large source: process in batches with bounded memory

Provide development-only catalogue fixtures for UI work, clearly separated from real data and impossible to load in production.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- backend/fixtures/dev_catalogue_sample.json (name must contain 'dev' and 'sample'); top-level field 'fixture_notice': 'Development fixture — not live Oriflame data'
- Fixture products use obviously placeholder names (e.g. 'Sample Product 01'), placeholder images served locally, and no real Oriflame SKUs or prices
- FixtureCatalogueSource refuses to load when APP_ENV=production
- Products loaded from fixtures get source_url pointing to a local placeholder and a flag/source value 'dev_fixture' so the UI can show a 'Development data' banner

EFFORT: S (3 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Backend / Fixtures
DEPENDENCIES: OR-013

TESTING CRITERIA:
- Loading fixtures with APP_ENV=production raises an error
- Fixture products are distinguishable via their source value
- Grep check: fixture file contains no real Oriflame product names, SKUs, or image URLs

EDGE CASES:
- Mixed real and fixture data in one database: fixture sync refused if real-source products exist (and vice versa) unless --force-dev is passed in development
- Fixture file missing or malformed: clear error, no partial load

- Prints run id, status, and counts; exit code 0 on success, non-zero on failed
- Documented in docs/guidence/try-it-locally.md and infrastructure/DEPLOYMENT.md
